etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English resolven, from Old French resolver, a learned borrowing of Latin resolvō (“loosen, thaw, melt, resolve”), equivalent to re- +‎ solve. Piecewise doublet of re-solve.
senses: (transitive) To find a solution to (a problem).
(transitive) To reduce to simple or intelligible notions; to make clear or certain; to unravel; to explain.
(countable) A determination to do something; a fixed decision.
